input.recap: ScubaGear's main path (at commit 9546152, 27 Oct 2026) no longer loads any module that needs Windows PowerShell 5.1. The 5.1-only rule now comes from the manifest, the docs and Windows-only CI. Nothing was changed in this repository.

content.text:
I cloned ScubaGear at commit `9546152` (27 Oct 2026, module v2.0.0) and checked the code. **Nothing in the module's main code path actually needs Windows PowerShell 5.1 any more.** It requires 5.1 because the manifest and docs say so, and the main path has two Windows-only parts (not 5.1-only).

**What enforces 5.1**
- **The module manifest:** `ScubaGear.psd1` sets `CompatiblePSEditions = 'Desktop'`, so PowerShell 7 refuses to import it without `-SkipEditionCheck`. It also sets `PowerShellVersion = '5.1'`, which is only a minimum.
- **The docs, which are out of date.** `docs/prerequisites/dependencies.md` says one Microsoft library is tied to PowerShell 5, and `docs/installation/psgallery.md` says some SharePoint modules don't work in PowerShell 7. That was true when ScubaGear used `Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell`, PnP, MicrosoftTeams, ExchangeOnlineManagement and the PowerApps module. Version 2.0 replaced all of them with direct REST calls (`SPORestHelper`, `TeamsRestHelper`, `EXORestHelper`, `PowerPlatformRestHelper`, `PowerBIRestHelper`). `RequiredVersions.ps1` now lists only `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` and `powershell-yaml`.
- **CI:** the smoke tests and PowerShell unit tests run on `windows-latest` with `shell: powershell`, so PowerShell 7 isn't tested end to end.

**What's only Windows (not only 5.1)**
1. **Certificate sign-in.** `ConnectHelpers.psm1:208` looks up the thumbprint in `Cert:\CurrentUser\My` and `Cert:\LocalMachine\My`. The `Cert:` drive exists in PowerShell 7 on Windows but not on macOS or Linux.
2. **Interactive sign-in.** `ConnectHelpers.psm1:268` calls MSAL with `WithUseEmbeddedWebView($true)`. An embedded web view works only on Windows, so on macOS or Linux the interactive sign-in for Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Power Platform and Power BI will most likely fail. The comment just above that line says to use the system browser, which is the opposite of what the code does. It looks like a bug.
3. **The configuration UI.** `ScubaConfigApp` uses WPF (`PresentationFramework`) in STA runspaces. That works in PowerShell 7 on Windows, but not on macOS or Linux. The docs already say the UI is Windows-only and point to `New-SCuBAConfig` elsewhere.

**What already handles PowerShell 7**
- **MSAL loading:** `Initialize-Msal` in `ConnectHelpers.psm1` has separate Desktop and Core branches. On 5.1 it forces MSAL to load by calling `Connect-MgGraph` with a fake thumbprint; on 7 it loads the DLL from the Graph module.
- **OPA:** the code picks the Windows, macOS or Linux OPA binary based on the operating system (`Support.psm1:393`, `ScubaConfigValidator.psm1`, `ScubaConfigDefaults.json`).
- **File encoding:** it writes `utf8NoBom` on PowerShell 6 and later (`Orchestrator.psm1:785`, `Diff.psm1:1070`).
- **Unit tests:** the config tests already have branches for Linux and macOS.

So with `-SkipEditionCheck`, a ScubaGear run should work in PowerShell 7 on Windows as long as nothing else breaks. To run it on macOS or Linux, it needs:
- a certificate passed some other way than a thumbprint in the store, or a client secret;
- the system browser for interactive sign-in;
- the manifest edition changed.

I read the code but didn't run ScubaGear in PowerShell 7, so this is from the source, not a test run.

input.recap: Interactive sign-in with -SkipEditionCheck on PowerShell 7 should fail for every product except Entra. ScubaGear asks MSAL for an embedded web view, and the .NET 6 MSAL that Graph auth ships for PowerShell 7 can't provide one. This is from reading the code and DLLs, not from a run.

content.text:
**No, not on PowerShell 7, even on Windows.** Interactive sign-in should break for every product except Entra. I worked this out by reading the code and the shipped DLLs; I haven't run it.

**Why it breaks**

ScubaGear signs in to each product in two ways:

- **Entra (AAD):** it calls `Connect-MgGraph` (`Connect-GraphIfNecessary` in `Connection.psm1`). That works in PowerShell 7, so the Entra checks would run.
- **Exchange, Defender/compliance, SharePoint, Teams, Power Platform and Power BI:** these get their tokens from ScubaGear's own `Get-MsalAccessToken` (`ConnectHelpers.psm1:167`). It calls MSAL directly, and its interactive branch (line 268) asks for an embedded web view:
  ```powershell
  $MsalApp.AcquireTokenInteractive(...).WithUseEmbeddedWebView($true)
  ```

On PowerShell 7, `Initialize-Msal` loads the MSAL DLL from the `Dependencies/Core` folder of `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication`. I downloaded version 2.25.0, the newest ScubaGear allows. Its Core MSAL is version 4.61.3 built for plain `net6.0`, not `net6.0-windows`. That build has no embedded browser, and the error text inside the DLL says so:

> "To enable the embedded webview on Windows, reference Microsoft.Identity.Client.Desktop and call … .WithWindowsEmbeddedBrowserSupport()"

The Graph auth package doesn't include `Microsoft.Identity.Client.Desktop`, and ScubaGear doesn't call that method. So on PowerShell 7 the first interactive token request should throw an `MsalClientException`. On macOS and Linux there's no embedded browser at all.

Silent sign-in won't save it. MSAL's token cache is in memory and starts empty in each session, so the first request for each client ID always goes to the interactive call.

**Why 5.1 works**

On 5.1, ScubaGear loads the `Desktop` MSAL, built for .NET Framework 4.6.2. That build has the old built-in Windows embedded browser, so this exact code works there. That's very likely the real reason ScubaGear still needs 5.1 for interactive runs.

**The fix would be small**

Change `WithUseEmbeddedWebView($true)` to `$false`, at least when `PSEdition` is `Core`. The system browser then signs in through `http://localhost`, which the code already sets as the redirect URI. The comment just above that line already says to use the system browser for passkeys, so `$true` looks like a mistake. Along with `-SkipEditionCheck`, this should make interactive runs work in PowerShell 7 on Windows, macOS and Linux. Certificate sign-in would still be Windows-only because of the `Cert:\` thumbprint lookup.

# Maester Packs that ship with Maester

Each folder here is a [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/packs) that is part of the Maester module:
a `maester-pack.json`, its suites of native tests, and its helpers and connectors.

- The build copies this folder to `packs/` in the module. A pack loads into its own private module from
  its folder; it is not compiled into `Maester.psm1`.
- A pack here is trusted as the module is: it needs no lock entry and no approval. It runs when its
  manifest says `"EnabledByDefault": true` unless the Maester config turns it off with
  `Packs: [{ "Id": "<id>", "Enabled": false }]`, and the other way round.
- Its ID is `maester.<name>`. Its `Code` is its own, such as `ZTA`. Because it is part of Maester, its test IDs
  have no `MP.` prefix: they are `ZTA.<n>` (or `ZTA` for a family), and its suite IDs start with `ZTA`. The code
  is added to the reserved prefixes in `powershell/assets/MaesterTestSchema.psd1`, so custom tests cannot use it. A pack installed later may not take a code that overlaps it. Its rows in the results have `Source = Custom` and a `Package`, so they never count as
  Maester's own checks.
- PowerShell Gallery modules it declares in `Uses.Modules` are pinned to one version. Users save them with
  `Install-MtPack <id>`, which records each module's digest in `maester-packs.lock.json`.

Check a pack with `Test-MtPack ./packs/<name> -Official` and run its tests with `Invoke-MtTest -Path ./packs/<name>`.

    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns one SCUBA.GWS instance per policy result in a ScubaGoggles ScubaResults file.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Instance source of the SCUBA.GWS family. Reads the ScubaResults JSON that the scubagoggles gws command wrote,

    the reason, when the setting is empty, the file is not found or the report is too old.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $reportPath = [string](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ScubaGoggles.ReportPath' -Default '')
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($reportPath)) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'No ScubaGoggles report to read. Run scubagoggles gws, then set the ScubaGoggles.ReportPath setting to the ScubaResults file or the folder it wrote.'
    }

    $file = Resolve-MtScubaGogglesResultFile -Path $reportPath
    $report = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file -Raw -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json -Depth 20
    if (-not $report.PSObject.Properties['Results'] -or -not $report.PSObject.Properties['MetaData']) {
        throw "$file is not a ScubaGoggles results file: it has no MetaData or Results."
    }
    if ([string]$report.MetaData.Tool -ne 'ScubaGoggles') {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "$file was written by $($report.MetaData.Tool), not ScubaGoggles."
    }

    $maxAgeDays = [int](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays' -Default 7)
    # ConvertFrom-Json reads the ISO date as a DateTime already; text is parsed invariantly, never in the current culture.

content.text:
Yes. After ScubaGear is imported, a pack can redefine `Get-MsalAccessToken` inside ScubaGear's own `ConnectHelpers` module so it opens the system browser instead of the embedded view. I tested this on mock modules laid out exactly like ScubaGear's, in pwsh 7.6. I couldn't test it on ScubaGear itself: importing the downloaded ScubaGear code was blocked by the auto-mode permission check.

**The patch**

```powershell
Import-Module ScubaGear -SkipEditionCheck

$helpers = Get-Module ConnectHelpers -All | Select-Object -First 1
& $helpers {
    $old  = 'WithUseEmbeddedWebView($true)'
    $body = ${function:script:Get-MsalAccessToken}.ToString()
    if (-not $body.Contains($old)) { throw 'Get-MsalAccessToken has changed upstream; the patch was not applied.' }
    # Run the definition inside this module so the new function belongs to it and can call its private helpers.
    . ([scriptblock]::Create("function script:Get-MsalAccessToken {`n$($body.Replace($old, 'WithUseEmbeddedWebView($false)'))`n}"))
}
# Modules that already imported the old copy take the patched one again.
foreach ($m in Get-Module -All | Where-Object { $_.ModuleType -eq 'Script' -and $_.Name -ne 'ConnectHelpers' }) {
    if (& $m { [bool](Get-Command Get-MsalAccessToken -CommandType Function -ErrorAction Ignore) }) {
        & $m { param($h) Import-Module $h -Function Get-MsalAccessToken } $helpers
    }
}
```

**Why it's written this way.** I tried two simpler versions first, and both failed in testing:
- **Assigning a new script block** to the function lost access to ScubaGear's private helpers such as `Initialize-Msal`, so it failed with "Initialize-Msal is not recognized". Running the function definition inside the module fixes that.
- **Patching only `ConnectHelpers`** didn't reach every caller:
  - `Connection.psm1` re-imports `ConnectHelpers` inside `Connect-Tenant` on every call, so it picks up the patch.
  - `ServicePrincipal.psm1` imports its own copy once, when ScubaGear loads, so it kept the old version until I re-imported it there.
- **The upstream check is deliberate.** The patch rewrites the function's current body rather than shipping a copy, and it throws if the line it replaces is gone. If CISA changes or fixes the function, the pack fails loudly instead of running stale code.
- The patch keeps `[CmdletBinding()]`, the parameter sets and the defaults.

**How I'd fit it into a pack:** run ScubaGear in a child `pwsh -NoProfile` process. That process imports ScubaGear, applies the patch, runs `Invoke-SCuBA` and writes its results file. The pack then reads that file, the same way the ScubaGoggles pack reads its report. I wouldn't run ScubaGear inside Maester's own process, because:
- ScubaGear allows `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` 2.0.0 to 2.25.0. Maester's session may already have a newer version loaded (2.41 on your machine), and only one version can load per process.
- ScubaGear calls `Connect-MgGraph` and `Disconnect-SCuBATenant`, which could replace or drop Maester's own Graph connection.
- Its startup scripts set `$Global:MaximumFunctionCount` and run a version check in the global scope.

The pack should also pin ScubaGear's version in `Uses.Modules`.

**Still to confirm:** applying the patch to the real ScubaGear and doing one actual interactive sign-in. The proper fix belongs upstream: a one-line change in `cisagov/ScubaGear` to `WithUseEmbeddedWebView($false)` on PowerShell 7, plus changing `CompatiblePSEditions`. The comment above that line already says to use the system browser, so they may well accept it.

=========== ISSUE #2545
ScubaGear 2.0.0 on PowerShell 7 / Linux: packaging and platform issues (with fixes) | OPEN | @directorcia | 2026-10-28 | labels: 
--- body:
I ran ScubaGear v2.0.0 under PowerShell 7.6.7 on Linux, using app-only certificate auth. Once the issues below were patched locally, it ran successfully for AAD, EXO, SecuritySuite, SharePoint and Teams. Here's what I found, with a suggested fix for each:

1. **The release zip uses backslash path separators.** On Linux it extracts to flat filenames like `ScubaGear\Modules\...` with broken permissions. Building the zip with forward slashes would fix it.
2. **The manifest is Desktop-only.** It sets `CompatiblePSEditions = 'Desktop'`. Adding `'Core'` would fix it.
3. **`Support.psm1` calls `WindowsPrincipal` five times.** Each call throws "Windows Principal functionality is not supported on this platform". Guarding the calls with `$IsWindows` would fix it.
4. **`ConnectHelpers.psm1` (around line 202) looks up certificates through the Windows-only `Cert:\` drive.** Using `[System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Store]::new('My','CurrentUser')` with `Find('FindByThumbprint', ...)` would work on every platform.
5. **There's a case mismatch on case-sensitive file systems.** `Orchestrator.psm1` (around line 1096) builds `SharePointConfig.rego`, but the file is named `SharepointConfig.rego`. Renaming the file or normalising the name would fix it.
6. **The dependency check gives false alarms on Linux.** It reports "OPA not installed" even though OPA is in `~/.scubagear/Tools`, reports the Graph module version wrongly, and calls `Get-CimInstance`, which fails on Linux. Making those checks platform-aware would fix it.
7. **Feature request: allow a separate app per product.** The single-app model means one service principal needs every product's permissions. Supporting a separate Graph app or certificate alongside the EXO, SharePoint and Teams credentials would help least-privilege setups.

--- body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This issue has an informative and human-readable title.

### 💡 Summary

I successfully ran ScubaGear 1.8.0 on Linux (Ubuntu 22.04) inside a Docker container using PowerShell 7.4, with AAD product fully working. Sharing this as a reference for the multi-platform effort.
What works:

AAD product, full authentication, provider execution, OPA Rego evaluation, JSON report output

What doesn't work (Linux X509Store limitation):

Teams and EXO certificate thumbprint auth fails with: "Unix LocalMachine X509Store is limited to the Root and CertificateAuthority stores."
This is a .NET/platform limitation, not a ScubaGear issue

How I got it working:
The blocker was [Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal] [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent() in Support.psm1 and related files, which throws on Linux. I worked around it by downloading the module source via Save-Module, patching out the Windows Principal calls with a Python regex script at Docker build time, then installing the patched version.
I also needed to:

Create a symlink opa → opa_linux_amd64_static since RunRego.psm1 looks for opa on non-Windows
Set $env:USERPROFILE = "/root" so ScubaGear resolves ~/.scubagear/Tools correctly
Pin MicrosoftTeams to 7.7.0 and Microsoft.Graph.Authentication to 2.25.0

The full Dockerfile, patch script, and run script are in this repo: https://github.com/TriagaSOAR/TriagaSOAR/tree/main/integrations/scubagear

Since #97 is now closed and #2062 moves SharePoint/PowerPlatform to REST calls, I expect most of these patches will become unnecessary in 1.9.0. The X509Store issue for Teams/EXO cert auth on Linux may still need addressing.

### Motivation and context

ScubaGear currently requires Windows, which prevents use in CI/CD pipelines, Docker-based SOC tooling, and Linux/Mac admin environments. Containerized deployment would make ScubaGear easier to integrate into automated security workflows without needing a Windows host.

### Implementation notes

1. I got ScubaGear 1.8.0 running on Ubuntu 22.04 in a Docker container using PowerShell 7.4. AAD product works fully, authentication, provider execution, OPA Rego evaluation, and JSON report output.

2. The blocker was [Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal] [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent() in Support.psm1 — throws on Linux. Workaround: patch source at build time with a Python regex script.

3. RunRego.psm1 looks for an executable named opa on non-Windows, a symlink from opa → opa_linux_amd64_static fixes it. 

4. $env:USERPROFILE must be set for OPA path resolution to work.

5. Teams/EXO cert auth fails with Unix LocalMachine X509Store is limited to Root and CertificateAuthority stores this is a .NET platform limitation.

6. Working Dockerfile and patch script: https://github.com/InfinitiWarrior/Splunk-Hackaton-Project/tree/main/integrations/scubagear

7. Related closed epic: #97. Most patches likely unnecessary once #2062 ships in a release.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ScubaGear can be run in a Docker container on Linux without source patching
- [ ] AAD product works with service principal + certificate auth on Linux
- [ ] Teams and EXO cert auth works on Linux (X509Store limitation resolved)

Multi-platform support | CLOSED | @schrolla | 2022-12-22 | labels: epic,enhancement
--- body:
# Description #

This epic focuses on updating ScubaGear so that it can be run on non-Windows platforms as well as on existing Windows platforms, but using PowerShell 7 rather than native PowerShell (i.e. PowerShell 5.1).  

Improvements for this epic include:
- Adding support under PowerShell 7 for ScubaGear
- Expanding use of appropriate platform executable when running OPA Rego
- Making any adjustments in supporting libraries or versions needed to support PS7 and other platforms

## Initiative / Goal ##

The goal is to make the tool function on multiple platforms so that the tool doesn't force a platform choice counter from the one users may have available.


## Hypothesis ##
By making the ScubaGear available to those running on non-Windows platforms, it will be possible to run the tool in environments where it was not previously possible or required setting up additional resources (like a Windows machine).  For example, it may allow for execution on non-Windows machines used as lightweight administrative boxes.

## Acceptance criteria ##

Criteria that are considered must have for feature launch and in-scope for this epic include:

- [ ] ScubaGear runs successfully under PowerShell 7 on Windows 10/11 platforms for all products
- [ ] ScubaGear runs successfully under PowerShell 7 on latest Mac OS platform with PowerShell installed for all products
- [ ] ScubaGear runs successfully under PowerShell 7 on current Linux platform with PowerShell installed for all products

## Stakeholders / Resources ##
Include CISA decision makers and dev team members in discussions about this epic.  Resources needed for this epic include access to test platforms (Win/Mac/Linux) to validate functional nature of tool.  May be able to use Github runners for some of those.

## Timeline ##
TBD

input.recap: No PR changes only the web view setting. The $true was set on purpose in a merged October PR, and the open MSAL rewrite PR switches to the system browser but still targets Windows and .NET Framework. Issue 2545 already lists the remaining PowerShell 7 and Linux problems.

content.text:
No PR changes only that setting. I need to correct what I said last time: `WithUseEmbeddedWebView($true)` isn't a mistake, CISA set it on purpose earlier this month. A large open PR switches back to the system browser.

**PRs that touch the web view setting**

- **[cisagov/ScubaGear#2464](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/pull/2464)**, merged 9 Oct, "Fix login auto detect M365Environment during interactive auth" (fixes [cisagov/ScubaGear#2460](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/2460)). It changed `WithUseEmbeddedWebView($false)` to `$true`. The team had switched to the system browser, and that broke the automatic detection of commercial, GCC and GCC High tenants in interactive runs on 5.1. Going back to the embedded window fixed it for the 2.0.0 release. The comment above the line was never updated, which is why it reads as if the code is wrong.
- **[cisagov/ScubaGear#2411](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/pull/2411)**, open, "Replace Graph Authentication module with bundled MSAL DLLs". This is the real change:
  - It drops the `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` dependency. ScubaGear would download MSAL 4.89.0 from NuGet on first use and check each DLL's hash and signature before loading it.
  - Interactive sign-in uses `WithUseEmbeddedWebView($false)` with a localhost redirect, and its docs say it never uses the embedded view or WAM. It redoes tenant detection so it works with the browser.
  - It's large, with 29 comments. Its review status is "changes requested", but a maintainer commented on 28 Oct that it would merge, and that the user on [cisagov/ScubaGear#1703](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/1703) should be told phishing-resistant MFA then works.
  - It doesn't change `CompatiblePSEditions = 'Desktop'`, keeps the `Cert:\` lookup, and downloads only the .NET Framework build of MSAL (`net462`). On PowerShell 7 it loads that same .NET Framework build. So it helps PowerShell 7 on Windows, but it isn't real cross-platform support.

**Issues about PowerShell 7 and non-Windows**

- **[cisagov/ScubaGear#2545](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/2545)**, opened 28 Oct by `directorcia` with no replies yet. They ran 2.0.0 on PowerShell 7.6 on Linux with certificate sign-in and got AAD, EXO, SecuritySuite, SharePoint and Teams working after patching:
  - the release zip, which uses backslash paths;
  - the manifest edition;
  - five `WindowsPrincipal` calls in `Support.psm1`;
  - the `Cert:\` lookup, using `X509Store('My','CurrentUser')` instead;
  - a file-name case mismatch (`SharePointConfig.rego` vs `SharepointConfig.rego`);
  - the dependency check, including its `Get-CimInstance` call.

  I'd missed the `WindowsPrincipal` calls and the case mismatch. They didn't test interactive sign-in, so the web view problem isn't on their list.
- **[cisagov/ScubaGear#2211](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/2211)**, open, Docker/Linux support. Two people ran 1.8.0 in Linux containers by patching the source at build time. One said all five products matched the Windows results. CISA replied in June that cross-platform support is on their radar, but first they need to finish the dependency work and test PowerShell 7 on Windows.
- **[cisagov/ScubaGear#1703](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/1703)**, open. Interactive sign-in fails when phishing-resistant MFA is enforced, because the embedded view on 5.1 can't do FIDO2 or passkeys. In July a maintainer said MSAL with the system browser on PowerShell 7 is the planned answer. PR #2411 is that answer.
- **[cisagov/ScubaGear#97](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/97)**, the multi-platform epic, closed in April 2026 to be split into smaller items. It's the history behind all of this, with old notes on the SharePoint and Power Platform modules and the same `.rego` case mismatch.

**What this means for the pack idea**

- **The patch hits a real trade-off.** On 5.1 it would bring back the bug that #2464 fixed. On PowerShell 7 it's needed, but tenant detection may still fail, so the pack should always pass `-M365Environment`.
- **Wait for #2411 before building the patch.** Once it merges, the browser fix is upstream and `Get-MsalAccessToken` is rewritten, so my patch's string check would fail anyway.
- **What a pack would still need after #2411:**
  - the manifest edition;
  - the `WindowsPrincipal` calls;
  - the `Cert:\` lookup;
  - the case mismatch.

  These are the #2545 items, and they're for non-Windows only. On Windows, `-SkipEditionCheck` alone would probably do, but I haven't run it.

Moving it to PowerShell 7 later needs a small pack change. It won't happen by itself. I also found that PowerShell 7 ignores ScubaGear's Desktop-only flag.
input.ask: Which shape should the ScubaGear pack take?

actions.label: Read reports first
actions.message: Build the ScubaGear pack as a report reader like the ScubaGoggles pack first; add launching ScubaGear later.

actions.label: Launch 5.1 too
actions.message: Build the ScubaGear pack so it reads reports and can also launch ScubaGear in a Windows PowerShell 5.1 child process on Windows.

content.text:
Mostly yes, with two catches.

**Catch 1: Maester can't run ScubaGear in its own process on 5.1.** Maester requires PowerShell 7.4 or later, and a pack loads into Maester's process. So a 5.1-only pack would have to work one of two ways:

- **Read a report** (the way the ScubaGoggles pack works). The user runs `Invoke-SCuBA` in Windows PowerShell 5.1 themselves, and the pack reads the `ScubaResults` JSON it wrote.
  - It works today, and Maester itself can run on any OS.
  - When ScubaGear starts working on PowerShell 7, the pack doesn't change at all. Users just run ScubaGear wherever they like.
- **Launch ScubaGear.** The pack starts a child `powershell.exe -NoProfile` process, which runs `Invoke-SCuBA` with an output folder, and then reads the results file.
  - On Windows that's ScubaGear's own tested setup, so interactive sign-in uses the embedded window that CISA tests.
  - One catch: `Install-MtPack` would install a pinned ScubaGear into the PowerShell 7 module folder (`Documents\PowerShell\Modules`). Windows PowerShell 5.1 only looks in `Documents\WindowsPowerShell\Modules`, so the child process must import ScubaGear by its full path.

**Catch 2: it won't start working on PowerShell 7 by itself.** The pack would pin a ScubaGear version, so a new ScubaGear release reaches users only when the pack updates its pin. Moving the launch to `pwsh` would be a small change to the pack. I'd build that in now as a setting, defaulting to `powershell.exe`, and switch the default once a ScubaGear release includes [cisagov/ScubaGear#2411](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/pull/2411).

After #2411, ScubaGear no longer needs `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication`. That removes the Graph module version clash with Maester, so running it inside Maester's own process becomes a real option. I'd still keep a separate process, because ScubaGear connects and disconnects Graph sessions and sets global variables. macOS and Linux would still need the fixes listed in [cisagov/ScubaGear#2545](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/2545), even after #2411.

**A correction:** you don't need `-SkipEditionCheck`. I tested a module whose manifest says `CompatiblePSEditions = 'Desktop'` in pwsh 7.6 on this Mac, and it imported without complaint. PowerShell 7 only checks that setting for modules in the Windows `System32` module folder, and ScubaGear is never installed there. So ScubaGear already imports in PowerShell 7 today. The interactive sign-in is what actually fails, not the import.

I'd start with the report reader, since it matches the ScubaGoggles pack and works now. The launcher can come later.

The plan once you choose where to build it:

116	function ConvertTo-MtZtaInstance {
117	    <#
118	    .SYNOPSIS
119	    Turns the Tests of a Zero Trust Assessment report into ZTA instances.
120	
121	    .DESCRIPTION
122	    The instance suffix is the assessment's test ID. A test that writes several rows under one ID (the Defender
123	    for Cloud recommendations do) gets a suffix made from a hash of each row's title, so a row keeps its ID from
124	    one run to the next. Rows that share a title as well are numbered in report order. Planned tests, which the assessment lists but has not built, are left out.
125	    #>
126	    [CmdletBinding()]
127	    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
128	    param(
129	        # A report read by Read-MtZtaReport.
130	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] $Report
131	    )
132	
133	    $severity = @{ High = 'High'; Medium = 'Medium'; Low = 'Low' }
134	    $rows = @($Report.Tests | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.TestStatus -ne 'Planned' -and $_.TestSkipped -ne 'UnderConstruction' })
135	    $repeated = @($rows | Group-Object -Property { [string]$_.TestId } | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object Name)
136	    $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
137	    $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
138	    try {
139	        foreach ($row in $rows) {
140	            $id = ([string]$row.TestId -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '_') -replace '^[^A-Za-z0-9]+', ''
141	            if (-not $id) { continue }
142	            if ([string]$row.TestId -in $repeated) {
143	                $hash = $sha.ComputeHash([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes([string]$row.TestTitle))
144	                $id = '{0}.{1}' -f $id, ([System.Convert]::ToHexString($hash).Substring(0, 10).ToLowerInvariant())
145	            }
146	            $unique = $id
147	            for ($n = 2; -not $seen.Add($unique); $n++) { $unique = "$id.$n" }
148	            $id = $unique
149	            $tags = @('ZeroTrust') + @(@($row.TestPillar) | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { "ZeroTrust.$_" })
150	            $instance = [ordered]@{
151	                Id    = $id
152	                Title = ([string]$row.TestTitle -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
153	                Tag   = $tags
154	                Data  = $row
155	            }
156	            if ($severity.ContainsKey([string]$row.TestRisk)) { $instance.Severity = $severity[[string]$row.TestRisk] }
157	            [pscustomobject]$instance
158	        }
159	    } finally {
160	        $sha.Dispose()
161	    }
162	}

167	    Runs the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment in a child PowerShell process and returns where it wrote its report.
168	
169	    .DESCRIPTION
170	    The assessment loads its own pinned versions of the Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online and Az modules and of
171	    MSAL, which cannot share a process with the versions Maester has already loaded. So it runs in its own
172	    pwsh process, signs in there with Connect-ZtAssessment, and Maester reads the report it writes.
173	
174	    The child's output is read line by line and shown with Write-MtTestOutput: in the dashboard of an
175	    interactive run it scrolls in a box in the main column, elsewhere it is written to the host. The
176	    assessment runs with -ShowLog (the ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog setting, on by default), so the box shows
177	    the tests it runs, and its progress bars become one line at the bottom of the box that updates in place.
178	
179	    The child also reports where the assessment is, read from the progress the module keeps for its own
180	    progress page and from the progress logs it writes: the stage, the exports or tests done of how many,
181	    the ones running, and each one that fails. It writes these as ##maester[progress] and ##maester[error]
182	    lines, which Write-MtTestOutput shows at the top of the box (see Write-MtTestProgress).
183	
184	    The child signs in to the tenant Maester is connected to. When Maester is connected to Graph app-only with a
185	    certificate, the child uses the same app and certificate; otherwise it signs in interactively. The
186	    ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect setting passes any other Connect-ZtAssessment parameters.

189	    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]

207	    $connect = [ordered]@{}

209	    $connectSetting = Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect' -Default $null

229	    }

276	    # Its output is read by Maester as lines of plain text. Its progress bars cannot be drawn there, so each

sidebar_position: 2
description: Create, check and publish a Maester Pack, with its manifest, tests, helpers and connector.

# Writing a pack

:::tip Guided setup
To make a pack without writing the files by hand, use the guided setup at
[packs.maester.cloud/publish](https://packs.maester.cloud/publish). It copies the
[demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo) into a repository of yours, or starts from an empty one,
and fills in the manifest, the pack's Guide, its tests and its banner from a form. Then it releases the pack and
publishes it. It writes the same files this page describes, so you can change any of them later by hand.
:::

A pack is a folder with a `maester-pack.json`. Create one with `New-MtPack`:

```powershell
New-MtPack -Path ./maester-google-workspace -Id contoso.google-workspace -Code CNT -Connector
Test-MtPack ./maester-google-workspace
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./maester-google-workspace
```

`Invoke-MtTest -Path` runs the pack from its folder, with its helpers and connector, and reloads it on every call.
`Test-MtPack` runs every check `Install-MtPack` runs, without installing: use it in the pack's own CI.

```text
maester-google-workspace/
  maester-pack.json
  README.md
  tests/
    suite.json
    Test.MP.CNT.1001.ps1
    Test.MP.CNT.1001.md
  helpers/
    Get-CntWorkspaceSetting.ps1
  connector/
    Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace.ps1
```

To share the pack, push the folder to a GitHub repository owned by the publisher and create a release. A release made
[immutable](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases) starts its
cooldown when it is published; any other release starts it when each user first sees it. To have it listed where
people look for packs, see [Publishing your pack](#publishing-your-pack).

## The manifest

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-1.0.json",
  "Id": "contoso.google-workspace",
  "Name": "Google Workspace checks",
  "Description": "Checks the security settings of a Google Workspace tenant.",
  "Version": "1.2.0",
  "Publisher": "contoso",
  "License": "MIT",
  "RequiresMaester": ">=3.0",
  "Code": "CNT",
  "Suites": ["tests"],
  "Helpers": ["helpers"],
  "Connectors": [
    {
      "Service": "CNT.GoogleWorkspace",
      "DisplayName": "Google Workspace",
      "File": "connector/Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace.ps1",
      "Connect": "Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace",
      "Test": "Test-CntGoogleWorkspace",
      "Disconnect": "Disconnect-CntGoogleWorkspace"
    }
  ],
  "Uses": {
    "Services": ["CNT.GoogleWorkspace"],
    "GraphScopes": [],
    "TenantWrites": [],
    "Network": ["admin.googleapis.com", "oauth2.googleapis.com"],
    "Modules": [ { "Name": "GoogleWorkspaceTools", "Version": "1.4.2" } ]
  }
}
```

| --- | --- |
| `$schema` | `https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-1.0.json`, so editors such as VS Code check the manifest as you type. Maester checks it again when the pack is installed and loaded. |
| `Id` | `<publisher>.<name>` in lower case. The publisher is the GitHub user or organisation that owns the repository; a pack whose publisher is not the repository owner is refused. |
| `Guid` | Required. A GUID that identifies the pack for good, such as `d1e2db80-6c27-4cb6-9389-2edf0a898d23`; `New-MtPack` makes one. Keep it, and the code, for every version of the pack: `Update-MtPack` refuses a release whose Guid or code changed. A pack with a new code is a new pack, with a new Guid. |
| `Version` | A semantic version, such as `1.2.0`. |
| `RequiresMaester` | The Maester versions the pack works with, such as `>=3.0`. Add an upper bound, such as `>=3.0 <4.0`, only if you know a later version breaks the pack. A pack that needs a newer Maester reports `RequiresNewerMaester`. `New-MtPack` fills in the version you made the pack with. |
| `Code` | The start of every test ID of the pack: `CNT` gives `MP.CNT.1001`. Two to ten letters or digits, starting with a letter. A publisher with several packs can group them with up to three parts separated by dots, such as `CNT.GWS` for `MP.CNT.GWS.1001`. No two installed packs may share a code, or have one code that starts with the other (`CNT` and `CNT.GWS`), so `Install-MtPack` refuses the second one. Any code is allowed, but pick one that the [Maester Packs site](https://packs.maester.cloud) does not list as claimed, so people can install your pack next to others. |
| `Suites` | Folders of native tests. Each needs a `suite.json` whose `Id` is the code or starts with it, such as `CNT.GoogleWorkspace`. |
| `Helpers` | Folders of `.ps1` files that hold functions the tests call. |
| `Connectors` | Services the pack connects to (below). |
| `Uses` | What the pack reaches, shown when it is installed. An unknown key under `Uses` is an error, so a pack cannot hide what it reaches behind a key an older Maester does not show. |
| `Uses.Modules` | PowerShell Gallery modules, each pinned to one exact `Version`. Maester saves them into its own store and checks their files before every load. A module the user installs themselves can only be run in a separate process: `{ "Name": "X", "MinimumVersion": "2.0.0", "Install": "User", "Process": "Child" }`. |
| `Requires.Packs` | Other packs this one needs: `{ "Id": "contoso.base", "Source": "contoso/maester-base", "Version": ">=1.0" }`. They are installed first, with their own approval. |
| `Exports` | Functions of this pack that packs requiring it may call. |
| `Pricing` | `Free` (the default) or `Paid`, for a pack that needs a paid product or subscription to be useful. The pack index shows it; Maester does not act on it. |
| `Banner` | An image in the pack that the pack index shows when it features the pack. See [Banner image](#banner-image). |
| `Guide` | A JSON file in the pack that says how to install, connect and run it, for its page on the pack index. See [The pack page](#the-pack-page). |
| `EnabledByDefault` | For a pack that ships with Maester: `false` to leave it off until the config turns it on. |

## Banner image

A banner is optional. When the maintainers feature a pack on [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud), the
card shows the banner beside the pack's description; without one, the card shows the pack's code and name on a dark
background.

- **File:** `.png`, `.jpg` or `.webp`, at most 1 MB, inside the pack, for example `"Banner": "assets/banner.png"`.
  The index reads the type from the file's contents, not its name, and SVG is refused. A banner that fails these
  checks is left out and the card falls back to the code and name.
- **Size:** 1200 × 630 pixels (the 1.91:1 shape of a social preview). Another size is cropped to fill that shape.
- **Shown small:** about 600 pixels wide on a desktop and 340 on a phone. Use at most eight words of text, set large,
  and keep it away from the edges.
- **Your own brand.** Use another company's logo only for a pack built on that company's product, and only with its
  permission. Don't add words such as "Official" or "Verified": the index shows its own badges, and a banner that
  suggests an endorsement it doesn't have can get the pack removed.
- **No secrets or real data:** a screenshot must not show a real tenant, user or key.

### Making one with an AI image tool

Any image tool that takes a text prompt can make a banner. Image tools often misspell words, so check every letter,
or ask for an image with no text and add the title yourself in an editor. Fill in the parts in angle brackets:

```text
A wide banner image, 1200 x 630 pixels, for a software add-on called "<pack name>".
It checks the security settings of <service, for example Google Workspace> for IT administrators.
Style: clean, modern, flat illustration on a <dark navy / deep teal / near-black> gradient background,
with a simple abstract motif suggesting <what the pack checks, for example identity, email, devices>.
Text: the title "<pack name>" in large, bold, white sans-serif letters on the left,
and the line "<one short phrase, at most six words>" below it in smaller letters.
Leave a margin of at least 60 pixels on every side. No other text, no logos, no people,
no photos of screens, no badges or seals.
```

For an image without text, replace the `Text:` line with `No text at all; leave the left half plain for a title.`

## The pack page

Every pack's page on [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud) has the same sections: Install, Connect,
Run, App-only, Tests, Security and Support. The index fills what it can from the manifest:

- the modules in `Uses.Modules`, with the line that installs each one;
- the Graph permissions in `Uses.GraphScopes`, which an app needs to run the pack app-only;
- the tests, with their products, from `Suites` (and `Catalog` for a family test that expands when it runs).

The rest comes from the Guide, a JSON file in the pack named by the manifest's `Guide` key, such as
`"Guide": "maester-pack.guide.json"`. Its schema is
[maester-pack-guide-1.0.json](https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json); add it as `$schema` so
editors check the file as you type. Commands in it are shown as text and never run. A short example:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json",
  "Summary": "Checks the security settings of Google Workspace.",
  "Prerequisites": [{ "Text": "A Google Workspace super admin account." }],
  "Connect": { "Steps": [{ "Text": "Connect Maester, then sign in to Google when asked", "Command": "Connect-Maester" }] },
  "Run": {
    "Commands": [{ "Text": "Only this pack", "Command": "Invoke-Maester -Pack CNT -SkipBuiltIn" }],
    "Options": [{ "Name": "GoogleWorkspace.Customer", "Default": "my_customer", "Text": "The customer ID to read." }]
  },
  "AppOnly": { "Supported": true, "Methods": { "Certificate": true, "ClientSecret": true }, "Text": "Use a service account key." },
  "Screenshots": [{ "Path": "assets/report.png", "Caption": "The pack's results in the Maester report" }],
  "Support": { "Pack": "https://github.com/contoso/maester-google-workspace/issues" }
}
```

Maester checks that the Guide is a JSON object and that its screenshots (at most six) are `.png`, `.jpg` or `.webp`
paths inside the pack. Like the banner, a screenshot that really is an image of at most 1 MB is not counted as
binary content. Any section can end with `"More": "<https link>"` to your own documentation. The
[Zero Trust Assessment pack's guide](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/packs/zero-trust-assessment/maester-pack.guide.json)
is a full example.

## Tests and helpers

A pack's tests are [native tests](../writing-tests/index.mdx) with IDs `MP.<Code>.<n>`, or `MP.<Code>` for a family whose instances add their own part. (Packs that ship with
Maester are part of it and drop the `MP.`: the Zero Trust Assessment pack's tests are `ZTA.<n>`.) Every `.ps1` in a suite
or helper folder holds only functions: code outside a function is refused, because it would run while the pack
loads. A pack loads into a private module of its own, so its tests can call its helpers and Maester's exported
commands. One pack does not see another pack's functions unless it requires that pack and the pack lists them in
`Exports`. This keeps cooperating packs from colliding; it is not a security boundary, because code in the same
PowerShell process can reach anything in it (see [Pack security](./security.md)).

The scan flags, and raises the risk of, what a reviewer should look at: binary files, dynamic code
(`Invoke-Expression`, `[scriptblock]::Create`), starting processes, requests to hosts that `Uses.Network` does not
list, and module imports that `Uses.Modules` does not list.

## Showing a long-running test's output and progress

A test that runs a tool for a long time, such as an assessment in another PowerShell process, can show the person
running Maester what the tool is doing while it runs. In the full-screen dashboard both go into a box in the main
column; in the compact layout, CI and redirected output they are written to the console, indented.

- `Write-MtTestOutput` shows the tool's log. `-Title` opens the box, each line
  scrolls into it, `-Progress` pins a changing line at the bottom, and `-Complete` closes it (Maester closes it when
  the test ends).
- `Write-MtTestProgress` shows where the tool is, as a header at the top of
  the box: the stage (`-Stage`, `-StageNumber`, `-StageCount`), a bar of the items done (`-Completed`, `-Total`,
  `-Failed`, `-Running`), what it is working on (`-Current`, `-Status`), and the errors it reported
  (`-ErrorMessage`), which the box also counts. With `-Stages` (the names of all the stages) the stages are drawn
  as a track, like the phases of a Maester run. With `-Items` (each with `Id`, and optionally `Title`, `Status`,
  `Detail` and `Seconds`) the box lists the items running and those that finished, with their result and time,
  the way the dashboard lists Maester's own tests; outside the dashboard each finished item is written once. Each
  call replaces the progress before it, so pass everything you know each time; a call with only `-ErrorMessage`
  keeps the progress.
- When the tool runs tests of its own, `-Results` (`Passed`, `Failed`, `Error`, `Investigate`, `Skipped`,
  `Running`, `Total` and optionally `Name`) and `-Groups` (the same counts with a `Name` each, such as the pillars
  of an assessment, with `-GroupLabel 'Zero Trust Pillars'`) show them in the dashboard in place of Maester's own while the
  box is open: in the Results panel and the result blocks, and where the products are listed. The times of the
  items that finished go into the Pace graph next to the logo and the Slowest panel.

```powershell
Write-MtTestOutput -Title 'Collecting the tenant data'
Write-MtTestProgress -Stage 'Exporting' -StageNumber 1 -StageCount 3 -Completed 12 -Total 40 -Running 2 -Current 'Users', 'Groups'
Write-MtTestProgress -ErrorMessage 'The export of Devices failed: Forbidden'
```

A tool in another process does not need to call Maester to report its progress. Pipe its output to
`Write-MtTestOutput`, and have it write lines of this form to standard output, from any language:

```text
##maester[progress] {"stages":["Export","Tests","Report"],"stageNumber":1,"stage":"Exporting","completed":12,"total":40,"failed":1,"items":[{"id":"Users","detail":"page 3","seconds":12},{"id":"Groups","status":"Passed","seconds":4.2}]}
##maester[progress] {"stage":"Running tests","results":{"passed":80,"failed":12,"running":4,"total":300},"groupLabel":"Zero Trust Pillars","groups":[{"name":"Identity","passed":50,"failed":8,"total":120}]}
##maester[error] The export of Devices failed: Forbidden
```

These lines set the header instead of showing in the log. The JSON object takes the names of the parameters of
`Write-MtTestProgress` in any case (`error` for `-ErrorMessage`), and leaves out what it does not know. Write a
`progress` line when something changes (at most a few times a second): each one is drawn. A line that cannot be read is dropped.

The [Zero Trust Assessment pack](./zero-trust-assessment.md) is a worked example: its child process reads the
progress the assessment keeps and the progress logs it writes, once a second, and writes these lines (see
`Invoke-MtZtaCollection` in `packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests/Test.ZTA.ps1`).

## Connectors

A connector adds a service to Maester. Its file holds a `Connect` and a `Test` function, and optionally
`Disconnect`, `Renew` and `Describe`:

```powershell
function Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string] $Domain, [string] $CredentialPath)

    $token = Get-CntAccessToken -Domain $Domain -CredentialPath $CredentialPath
    Set-MtConnectionState -Value @{ Token = $token.AccessToken; ExpiresOn = $token.ExpiresOn } -Tenant $Domain
}

function Test-CntGoogleWorkspace {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()
    [bool](Get-MtConnectionState)
}
```

- `Connect-Maester -Service CNT.GoogleWorkspace` calls `Connect` with the parameters it has from `-ServiceSetting`,
  `MAESTER_CNT_GOOGLEWORKSPACE_<PARAMETER>` and `Connections.CNT.GoogleWorkspace` in the config.
- `Set-MtConnectionState` keeps what the tests need for the PowerShell session only; `Get-MtConnectionState`
  reads it back in a test or helper. A pack can read its own connection and those of packs it requires, never
  another pack's.
- `Test` decides whether the tests that need the service run. With `ExpiresOn` in the state, Maester calls `Renew`
  shortly before it expires.
- The service name is `<Code>.<Name>`. Tests declare it like any service: `Service = 'CNT.GoogleWorkspace'`.
  `"OptIn": true` makes its tests not run, rather than skipped, while it is not connected.

## Publishing your pack

Once the pack has a release, anyone can install it from its repository with `Install-MtPack <owner>/<repo>`. To
help people find it, list it on a pack index: a site that collects packs, checks them and shows each one's page.
An index only lists a pack. People still install it straight from your repository, and Maester runs the same checks
at install whichever site they found it on.

### Maester Packs

[packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud/) is the index the Maester team runs. To list a pack there:

1. Go to [packs.maester.cloud/publish](https://packs.maester.cloud/publish) and choose
   **Yes, I have a pack repository**.
2. Sign in with GitHub as an admin of the repository. The repository must be public; private and internal
   repositories are never listed.
3. Pick the repository, and the folder if the pack is not at its root, then press **Check**. It reads the latest
   release and its `maester-pack.json`, and says what to fix.
4. Press **Publish**. The site registers the pack's `Guid` and `Code` to the repository's owner, so nobody else can
   publish a pack with them, and queues the pack.

Within about ten minutes the index runs `Test-MtPack`'s checks and its security scan on the release and lists the
pack, with its page at `/p/<code>`. If the pack is not listed, its status page at `/status/<owner>/<repo>` says why
and what to fix. Every later release is picked up on its own, so you publish only once. **My Packs** on the site
shows your packs and how many tenants run them, and lets you hide one from the site for a while.

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes the test catalog of the Zero Trust Assessment pack from a copy of the ZeroTrustAssessment module.

.DESCRIPTION
Reads the [ZtTest] attribute of every Test-Assessment.<id>.ps1 in the module's tests folder from the syntax tree
(nothing is run), applies the titles and ratings of the module's TestMeta.json the way the assessment does, and
writes packs/zero-trust-assessment/catalog.json: the module version it was built from and one entry per test.

The catalog lists what the pack can report before any run: the test IDs, titles and ratings shown in the
pack's listing. Results at run time come from the assessment's report, so a test added in a newer version of
the module is still reported; rerun this script when the pack moves to a new version.

.PARAMETER SourcePath
The ZeroTrustAssessment module folder (the one that holds ZeroTrustAssessment.psd1), or a clone of
https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment. Defaults to the newest installed version of the module.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Where to write the catalog. Defaults to packs/zero-trust-assessment/catalog.json in this repository.

.EXAMPLE
./build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1

.EXAMPLE
./build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/zerotrustassessment
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $SourcePath,

    [string] $OutputPath = (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..', 'packs', 'zero-trust-assessment', 'catalog.json')
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not $SourcePath) {
    $installed = Get-Module -Name ZeroTrustAssessment -ListAvailable | Sort-Object -Property Version -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $installed) { throw 'The ZeroTrustAssessment module is not installed. Install it, or pass -SourcePath.' }
    $SourcePath = $installed.ModuleBase
}
$manifestPath = @(
    (Join-Path $SourcePath 'ZeroTrustAssessment.psd1'),
    (Join-Path -Path $SourcePath -ChildPath 'src' -AdditionalChildPath 'powershell', 'ZeroTrustAssessment.psd1')
) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $manifestPath) { throw "No ZeroTrustAssessment.psd1 under $SourcePath." }
$moduleRoot = Split-Path -Parent $manifestPath
$manifest = Import-PowerShellDataFile -LiteralPath $manifestPath
$testsPath = Join-Path $moduleRoot 'tests'

$meta = @{}
$metaPath = Join-Path $testsPath 'TestMeta.json'
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $metaPath) {
    $json = Get-Content -LiteralPath $metaPath -Raw -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
    foreach ($key in $json.Keys) { $meta[[string]$key] = $json[$key] }
}

function ConvertFrom-MtZtaAttributeValue {
    param($Ast)
    switch ($Ast.GetType().Name) {
        'StringConstantExpressionAst' { return $Ast.Value }
        'ConstantExpressionAst' { return $Ast.Value }
        'ExpandableStringExpressionAst' { return $Ast.Value }
        'ParenExpressionAst' { return ConvertFrom-MtZtaAttributeValue $Ast.Pipeline.PipelineElements[0].Expression }
        'ArrayLiteralAst' { return @($Ast.Elements | ForEach-Object { ConvertFrom-MtZtaAttributeValue $_ }) }
        'VariableExpressionAst' { return [bool]($Ast.VariablePath.UserPath -eq 'true') }
        default { return $Ast.Extent.Text }
    }
}

$tests = foreach ($file in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $testsPath -Filter 'Test-Assessment.*.ps1' | Sort-Object Name) {
    $ast = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($file.FullName, [ref]$null, [ref]$null)
    $attribute = $ast.Find({
            param($node)
            $node -is [System.Management.Automation.Language.AttributeAst] -and $node.TypeName.Name -eq 'ZtTest'
        }, $true)
    if (-not $attribute) {
        Write-Warning "$($file.Name) has no [ZtTest] attribute; skipped."
        continue
    }
    $values = @{}
    foreach ($argument in $attribute.NamedArguments) {
        $values[$argument.ArgumentName] = ConvertFrom-MtZtaAttributeValue $argument.Argument
    }
    $id = [string]$values.TestId
    # TestMeta.json is what the assessment itself shows; it wins over the attribute, as in Add-ZtTestResultDetail.
    foreach ($key in 'Title', 'Category', 'Pillar', 'RiskLevel', 'UserImpact', 'ImplementationCost', 'SfiPillar', 'TenantType', 'MinimumLicense') {
        if ($meta.ContainsKey($id) -and $meta[$id].ContainsKey($key) -and $meta[$id][$key]) { $values[$key] = $meta[$id][$key] }
    }
    [ordered]@{
        Id                 = "ZTA.$id"
        TestId             = $id
        Title              = (([string]$values.Title) -replace "''", "'" -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
        Pillar             = @($values.Pillar | Where-Object { $_ })
        Category           = [string]$values.Category
        Severity           = if ([string]$values.RiskLevel -in 'High', 'Medium', 'Low') { [string]$values.RiskLevel } else { $null }
        UserImpact         = [string]$values.UserImpact
        ImplementationCost = [string]$values.ImplementationCost
        Service            = @($values.Service | Where-Object { $_ })
        License            = @(@($values.CompatibleLicense) + @($values.MinimumLicense) | Where-Object { $_ } | Select-Object -Unique)
        TenantType         = @($values.TenantType | Where-Object { $_ })
    }
}

$catalog = [ordered]@{
    '$comment'   = 'Generated by build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1 from the ZeroTrustAssessment module (MIT licence, (c) Microsoft Corporation). Do not edit by hand.'
    Module       = 'ZeroTrustAssessment'
    ModuleVersion = [string]$manifest.ModuleVersion
    Source       = 'https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment'
    Tests        = @($tests | Sort-Object { [int]$_.TestId })
}
$catalog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $OutputPath -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Information -InformationAction Continue -MessageData "Wrote $(@($tests).Count) tests from ZeroTrustAssessment $($manifest.ModuleVersion) to $OutputPath."
# Maintaining the Zero Trust Assessment pack

The pack is in [`packs/zero-trust-assessment`](../../packs/zero-trust-assessment).

`catalog.json` lists the assessment's tests, titles and ratings for the pack's listing. It is generated; do not
edit it. To move the pack to a new version of the module, run:

```powershell
./build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath <ZeroTrustAssessment module folder or repository clone>
```

The live progress in Maester's output box depends on two things in the module, which a new version can change:
the `ZtAssessment.ProgressState` dictionary (`_stageName`, `_stageNumber`, `_totalStages`, `_totalItems`,
`_completedItems`, `_failedItems`, `_inProgressItems` and the `worker_*` entries) and the lines of
`zt-export/logs/<run>/1-export_progress.log`, `2-database_progress.log` and `3-test_progress.log`. When you move
the pack to a new version, run it once and check that the box still shows the stage and the counts.

Some checks produce one result per item: per drift folder, per recommendation, per user. Declare
`InstanceSource` with the name of a function in the same file. The engine calls that function when the test
runs (never during discovery) and runs the test once per object it returns, passing the object as `$Instance`.

```powershell
function Get-ContosoAdminUnit {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    foreach ($unit in Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'directory/administrativeUnits') {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id    = $unit.id                     # required: the instance suffix
            Title = "Administrative unit '$($unit.displayName)' is restricted"   # optional
            Data  = $unit                        # optional: anything the test needs
        }
    }
}

function Test-ContosoAdminUnitRestricted {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CONTOSO.2001',
        Title = 'Administrative units are restricted.',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        Service = 'Graph',
        InstanceSource = 'Get-ContosoAdminUnit'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The administrative unit to check, supplied by the engine.
        $Instance
    )

    $restricted = [bool]$Instance.Data.isMemberManagementRestricted
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Member management restricted: $restricted"
    return $restricted
}
```

The instance object has:

| Property | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | Yes | The suffix. The row's ID is `<parent ID>.<Id>`, for example `CONTOSO.2001.4f6c...`. It must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$` and be unique within the family. |
| `Title` | No | The instance's title. Defaults to `-TestTitle` from the helper, then the attribute's title. |
| `Severity` | No | The instance's severity, used when the config sets none. |
| `Tag` | No | Extra tags written to the instance's row. |
| `Data` | No | Anything the test needs. |

Each instance row carries `ParentId` (the family's ID) and `InstanceId`. When the family does not produce
instance rows, the result has one row on the parent ID instead:

| What happened | Row on the parent ID |
| --- | --- |
| The family was not selected, was disabled, or a gate failed | The usual `NotRun` or `Skipped` reason |
| The instance source returned nothing | `Skipped` with `NoInstances` |
| The instance source threw, did not finish within the family's timeout, or ended with `exit` | `Error` with `InstanceSourceFailed` |
| An instance `Id` is missing, invalid or repeated | `Error` with `InvalidInstanceId` |

The instance source runs under the same timeout as the test (the family's `TimeoutSeconds`, or the run's
`Execution` timeout). The source gets that long to return, and then each instance gets that long to run.

Selection and configuration understand families:

- `-TestId CONTOSO.2001` or `-TestId 'CONTOSO.2001.*'` selects the whole family.
- `-TestId CONTOSO.2001.abc` runs only that instance; the others get `NotRun` rows with reason `NotSelected`.

# Schema of the [MaesterTest] attribute (docs/proposals/maester-3.0-test-attributes.md, section 2, and
# the Maester 3.0 design, sections 3.1 and 4).
#
# The engine reads [MaesterTest(...)] from a test file's AST and validates it against this table;
# a test file is never executed to read its metadata. The property list must match
# MaesterTestAttribute in src/Maester.Engine (a unit test compares them).
#
# Property keys:
#   Type             string | string[] | bool
#   Required         Always | BuiltIn (required for tests shipped with Maester) | No
#   NotRequiredWhen  the property is not required when another property has this value, for example
#                    @{ Severity = 'Info' }
#   AllowedValues    closed list, compared case-insensitively and stored in this spelling
#   ValuesFrom       the values are validated against an engine registry instead of a fixed list:
#                    ServiceRegistry, or Taxonomy.Products, Taxonomy.Features, Taxonomy.Areas and
#                    Taxonomy.ResourceTypes (assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1). A test shipped with Maester must
#                    use a registry value; a custom test may use any value that fits Pattern and MaxLength
#   Pattern          regular expression each value must match
#   MaxLength        maximum length of each value
#   Default          value used when the property is omitted (documentation; the engine applies it)
#   Description      one line, used by generated docs
@{
    SchemaVersion    = '1.0'

    # Segments of letters and digits (and '_' after the first segment) separated by '.' or '-',
    # starting with a letter and containing at least one digit or separator.
    IdPattern        = '^(?=.*[0-9.\-])[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*([.\-][A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$'
    IdMaxLength      = 64

title: Zero Trust Assessment pack

description: Run Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment from Maester and see each of its results in the Maester report.

# Zero Trust Assessment pack

This pack runs Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) and shows each of its
results in the Maester report, next to Maester's own checks. It ships with Maester and does not run unless you
ask for it.

Each assessment result is one row, `ZTA.<assessment test ID>` (for example `ZTA.21770`), with the
assessment's title, risk level (as the severity), description, remediation steps and findings. Results are tagged
`ZeroTrust` and `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` (`ZeroTrust.Identity`, `ZeroTrust.Devices` and so on).

The pack's ID is `maester.zero-trust-assessment`. It needs no `Install-MtPack`: it is part of the Maester module,
and `Get-MtPack` lists it.

## Run it

Install the assessment's module once, connect Maester to the tenant, then name the pack:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -SkipBuiltIn    # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA                 # Maester's tests and the assessment
```

You don't run `Connect-ZtAssessment` yourself. The assessment runs in a separate PowerShell process, which can't
use the sign-ins of your session, so Maester signs in there for you (see
[Let Maester run the assessment](#let-maester-run-the-assessment)). After an interactive `Connect-Maester` you
sign in a second time, in the browser, for the assessment. `Connect-Maester` is still needed: it tells the
assessment which tenant to sign in to, and the pack is skipped while Maester is not connected to Graph. If you
read a report you already have (below), you run `Connect-ZtAssessment` and `Invoke-ZtAssessment` yourself first.

The pack is a long-running test, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless you name it. These also run it:

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -TestId ZTA          # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Suite ZTA              # the same
Invoke-Maester -IncludeLongRunning          # everything, including the assessment
```

The pack itself stays enabled, so naming it is enough; it is the long-running flag that keeps it out of a plain
`Invoke-Maester`. To remove it entirely, set `Packs: [{ "Id": "maester.zero-trust-assessment", "Enabled": false }]`.

To run it on every run, add it to `Selection.TestId` in `maester-config.json`, or set
`Selection.IncludeLongRunning` to `true`. Give it time with `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`: the assessment
can take an hour or more on a large tenant.

The pack gets the assessment's results one of two ways.

### Read a report you already have (recommended in CI)

Run the assessment as its own step, then point Maester at the report it wrote:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
used, because Maester cannot redact the assessment's report.

## Settings

All settings go in `GlobalSettings` of `maester-config.json`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` | empty | Read this report instead of running the assessment. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` | `7` | Refuse a report older than this. `0` turns the check off. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport` | `true` | Embed the assessment's own HTML report in the Maester report. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` | temporary | Where the assessment writes its report and export. Kept when set. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Pillar` | `All` | Run one pillar only: `Identity`, `Devices`, `Network`, `Data`, `Infrastructure`, `SecOps` or `AI`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Tests` | all | Run only these assessment test IDs, for example `["21770", "21771"]`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Days` | `30` | Days of sign-in logs the assessment reads (1 to 30). |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog` | `true` | Run the assessment with `-ShowLog`, which lists the tests it runs in its live output. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.DisableTelemetry` | `true` | The assessment sends the tenant ID to Microsoft unless this is `true`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` | none | Further `Connect-ZtAssessment` parameters, for example `{ "Service": ["Graph", "Azure"], "UseDeviceCode": true }`. |

`EmergencyAccessAccounts` is passed to the assessment as well, so its Conditional Access tests leave out the same
break-glass accounts as Maester's.

## How results map

| Assessment status | Maester result |
| --- | --- |
| Passed | Passed |
| Failed | Failed |
| Investigate | Investigate |
| Skipped | Skipped, with the assessment's reason |
| Error | Error |
| Planned | Not shown: the assessment has not built the test yet |

A test that writes several rows under one ID (the Defender for Cloud recommendations) gets one row each, with a
suffix made from the row's title so that it keeps its ID from run to run.

## Licence

The Zero Trust Assessment is © Microsoft Corporation and published under the
[MIT licence](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment/blob/main/LICENSE). This pack does not include
its code: it runs the module you install, or reads the report it wrote.

content.text: Writing the catalog builder first. It reads ScubaGear's `ScubaBaselines.json` (plain data; nothing from ScubaGear is run).

input.content:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes the policy catalog of the ScubaGear pack from a copy of CISA's ScubaGear module.

.DESCRIPTION
Reads schemas/ScubaBaselines.json, the baselines ScubaGear ships as data, and the module version from
ScubaGear.psd1 (nothing is run), and writes packs/scubagear/catalog.json: the module and baseline versions it was
built from and one entry per policy.

The catalog lists what the pack can report before any run: the policy IDs, titles and criticality shown in the
pack's listing. The pack also reads each policy's rationale and implementation steps from it, for the
description and remediation of a result. Results at run time come from ScubaGear's ScubaResults file, so a policy
added in a newer version of ScubaGear is still reported; rerun this script when the pack moves to a new version.

.PARAMETER SourcePath
The ScubaGear module folder (the one that holds ScubaGear.psd1), or a clone of
https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear. Defaults to the newest installed version of the module.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Where to write the catalog. Defaults to packs/scubagear/catalog.json in this repository.

.EXAMPLE
./build/scubagear/Update-MtScubaGearCatalog.ps1

.EXAMPLE
./build/scubagear/Update-MtScubaGearCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGear
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $SourcePath,

    [string] $OutputPath = (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..', 'packs', 'scubagear', 'catalog.json')
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not $SourcePath) {
    $installed = Get-Module -Name ScubaGear -ListAvailable | Sort-Object -Property Version -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $installed) { throw 'The ScubaGear module is not installed. Install it, or pass -SourcePath.' }
    $SourcePath = $installed.ModuleBase
}
$manifestPath = @(
    (Join-Path $SourcePath 'ScubaGear.psd1'),
    (Join-Path -Path $SourcePath -ChildPath 'PowerShell' -AdditionalChildPath 'ScubaGear', 'ScubaGear.psd1')
) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $manifestPath) { throw "No ScubaGear.psd1 under $SourcePath." }
$moduleRoot = Split-Path -Parent $manifestPath
$manifest = Import-PowerShellDataFile -LiteralPath $manifestPath
$baselinesPath = Join-Path -Path $moduleRoot -ChildPath 'schemas' -AdditionalChildPath 'ScubaBaselines.json'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $baselinesPath)) { throw "No schemas/ScubaBaselines.json under $moduleRoot; ScubaGear 2.0 or later is needed." }
$baselines = Get-Content -LiteralPath $baselinesPath -Raw -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json

# ScubaGear's product keys, as its results name them, in the order its report shows them.
$products = [ordered]@{
    aad           = 'AAD'
    exo           = 'EXO'
    securitysuite = 'SecuritySuite'
    sharepoint    = 'SharePoint'
    teams         = 'Teams'
    powerplatform = 'PowerPlatform'
    powerbi       = 'PowerBI'
}

$tests = foreach ($key in $baselines.baselines.PSObject.Properties.Name) {
    $product = if ($products.Contains($key)) { $products[$key] } else { $key }
    foreach ($policy in @($baselines.baselines.$key)) {
        $controlId = [string]$policy.id
        if ($controlId -notmatch '^(MS\.[A-Z]+\.\d+\.\d+)v\d+$') {
            Write-Warning "$controlId is not a ScubaGear policy ID such as MS.AAD.1.1v1; skipped."
            continue
        }
        $criticality = ([string]$policy.criticality).Trim()
        [ordered]@{
            Id             = "SCUBA.M365.$($Matches[1])"
            ControlId      = $controlId
            Product        = $product
            Title          = (([string]$policy.name) -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
            Section        = ([string]$policy.policySection).Trim()
            Criticality    = $criticality
            Severity       = if ($criticality -like 'SHALL*') { 'High' } else { 'Medium' }
            Badges         = @($policy.badges | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.label } | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.label })
            # The technique IDs only, such as T1110.001, from names such as 'T1110.001: Password Guessing'.
            Mitre          = @($policy.mitreMapping | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.Name -match '^(T\d{4}(?:\.\d{3})?)\b' } | ForEach-Object { ($_.Name -split ':')[0].Trim() } | Select-Object -Unique)
            License        = @($policy.licenseRequirements | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -ne 'N/A' } | ForEach-Object { ([string]$_).Trim() })
            Rationale      = ([string]$policy.rationale).Trim().Trim('"').Trim()
            Implementation = ([string]$policy.implementation).Trim().Trim('"').Trim()
            Notes          = @($policy.notes | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { ([string]$_).Trim() })
            Resources      = @($policy.resources | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.Url } | ForEach-Object { [ordered]@{ Name = (([string]$_.Name) -replace '\\\|', '|' -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim(); Url = [string]$_.Url } })
        }
    }
}

$catalog = [ordered]@{
    '$comment'      = 'Generated by build/scubagear/Update-MtScubaGearCatalog.ps1 from the ScubaGear module (CC0 1.0, CISA). Do not edit by hand.'
    Module          = 'ScubaGear'
    ModuleVersion   = [string]$manifest.ModuleVersion
    BaselineVersion = ([string]$baselines.Version -split ' ')[0]
    Source          = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear'
    Tests           = @($tests)
}
$catalog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $OutputPath -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Information -InformationAction Continue -MessageData "Wrote $(@($tests).Count) policies from ScubaGear $($manifest.ModuleVersion) (baselines $($catalog.BaselineVersion)) to $OutputPath."

# CISA ScubaGear for Microsoft 365

A Maester Pack that ships with Maester. It runs CISA's [ScubaGear](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear), or reads
the results it wrote, and shows each policy result in the Maester report as `SCUBA.M365.<policy ID>`, for example
`SCUBA.M365.MS.AAD.1.1`.

- `maester-pack.json` declares the pack (`maester.scubagear`, code `SCUBA.M365`). It is off by default.
- `tests/Test.SCUBA.M365.ps1` is one family test. Its instance source reads ScubaGear's `ScubaResults_<id>.json`
  from the `ScubaGear.ReportPath` setting, or runs `Invoke-SCuBA` in a separate Windows PowerShell process and reads
  the results it writes.
- `catalog.json` lists ScubaGear's policies, with their titles, criticality, rationale and remediation steps. It is
  generated by [`build/scubagear/Update-MtScubaGearCatalog.ps1`](../../build/scubagear/README.md); do not edit it.

How to run it, its settings and how results map: [maester.dev/docs/packs/scubagear](https://maester.dev/docs/next/packs/scubagear).

ScubaGear is published by CISA under [CC0 1.0](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/LICENSE). This pack
does not include its code: it runs the module you install, or reads the results it wrote.

input.content:
# Maintaining the ScubaGear pack

The pack is in [`packs/scubagear`](../../packs/scubagear).

`catalog.json` lists ScubaGear's policies, titles, criticality, rationale and remediation steps, for the pack's
listing and for the description of each result. It is generated from `schemas/ScubaBaselines.json` in the ScubaGear
module; do not edit it. To move the pack to a new version of ScubaGear, run:

```powershell
./build/scubagear/Update-MtScubaGearCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath <ScubaGear module folder or repository clone>
```

The pack reads these parts of ScubaGear's `ScubaResults_<id>.json`, which a new version can change: `MetaData`
(`Tool`, `TenantId`, `TimestampZulu`) and `Results.<product>[].Controls[]` (`Control ID`, `Requirement`, `Result`,
`Criticality`, `Details`, `IncorrectResult`), with the result values `Pass`, `Fail`, `Warning`, `N/A`, `Omitted`,
`Incorrect result`, `Error` and `-`.

ScubaGear 2.0 runs only in Windows PowerShell 5.1: in PowerShell 7 its interactive sign-in asks MSAL for an embedded
web view, which the .NET build of MSAL does not have. CISA's
[cisagov/ScubaGear#2411](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/pull/2411) moves it to the system browser. When a
release with that change is out, test it with `ScubaGear.PowerShell` set to `pwsh`, and consider making `pwsh` the
default.
