---
title: ScubaGear pack
sidebar_position: 5
description: Run CISA's ScubaGear from Maester, or read its results, and see each of its policy results in the Maester report.
---

# ScubaGear pack

This pack runs CISA's [ScubaGear](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear), or reads the results it wrote, and shows
each policy result in the Maester report, next to Maester's own checks. ScubaGear checks a Microsoft 365 tenant
against CISA's [Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA)](https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/services/secure-cloud-business-applications-scuba-project)
baselines for Entra ID, Exchange Online, Defender and Purview, SharePoint, Teams, Power Platform and Power BI.

Each policy result is one row, `SCUBA.M365.<policy ID>` (for example `SCUBA.M365.MS.AAD.1.1`), with the policy's
requirement as its title, its rationale and remediation steps, and ScubaGear's findings. A `SHALL` policy has the
severity High and a `SHOULD` policy Medium. Results are tagged `SCuBA`, `SCuBA.<product>` (`SCuBA.AAD`,
`SCuBA.EXO` and so on) and, for a policy that BOD 25-01 requires, `BOD25-01`.

The ID leaves out the policy's version (`v1`), so a row keeps its ID when CISA revises a policy. Maester's own
[CISA tests](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/cisa/) check some of the same policies in Maester's way; this pack
shows ScubaGear's own results.

The pack's ID is `maester.scubagear`. It ships with Maester and is off by default. Turn it on in
`maester-config.json`:

```json
{
  "Packs": [{ "Id": "maester.scubagear", "Enabled": true }]
}
```

## Run it

The pack gets ScubaGear's results one of two ways.

### Read results you already have

Run ScubaGear as its own step, on Windows, then point Maester at what it wrote. Maester can then run on any
platform.

```powershell
# In Windows PowerShell 5.1
Invoke-SCuBA -OutPath C:\scuba -Quiet

# In PowerShell 7, anywhere
Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.M365
```

with `ScubaGear.ReportPath` set to the `ScubaResults_<id>.json` file, the run's `M365BaselineConformance_<time>`
folder, or the `-OutPath` folder, where the newest run wins:

```json
{
  "GlobalSettings": { "ScubaGear.ReportPath": "C:\\scuba" }
}
```

The pack refuses results older than seven days (`ScubaGear.MaxReportAgeDays`), and results for another tenant
than the one Maester is connected to.

### Let Maester run ScubaGear

On Windows, with `ScubaGear.ReportPath` empty, the pack runs `Invoke-SCuBA` itself. ScubaGear 2.0 runs only in
Windows PowerShell 5.1, and Maester in PowerShell 7, so the pack starts a separate Windows PowerShell process for
it and reads the results it writes. Install ScubaGear there once:

```powershell
# In Windows PowerShell 5.1
Install-Module ScubaGear -Scope CurrentUser
Initialize-SCuBA
```

Then run Maester as usual, in PowerShell 7:

```powershell
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.M365 -SkipBuiltIn    # only ScubaGear
Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.M365                 # Maester's tests and ScubaGear
```

ScubaGear signs in in its own process:

- **Interactively:** it opens its own sign-in window for the products it checks. `Connect-Maester` is not needed
  for this, but with it the pack checks that ScubaGear's results are for the same tenant.
- **App-only:** when Maester is connected to Graph app-only with a certificate in the Windows certificate store,
  ScubaGear uses the same app and certificate, and the tenant's initial domain. Give the app the permissions and
  roles ScubaGear's [non-interactive guide](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/docs/prerequisites/noninteractive.md)
  lists. Without a certificate (a client secret, a managed identity or workload identity federation) the pack is
  skipped, because ScubaGear signs in app-only only with a certificate.

The pack is a long-running test, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless you name it with `-Pack`, `-TestId
SCUBA.M365` or `-IncludeLongRunning`. ScubaGear can take half an hour or more on a large tenant; give it time with
`Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`. Its output shows in Maester's console while it runs.

On macOS and Linux the pack does not run ScubaGear: read results you already have instead. ScubaGear 2.0 does not
run in PowerShell 7, because its sign-in window needs Windows PowerShell. When a version of ScubaGear runs in
PowerShell 7, set `ScubaGear.PowerShell` to `pwsh`.

## Settings

All settings go in `GlobalSettings` of `maester-config.json`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScubaGear.ReportPath` | empty | Read these results instead of running ScubaGear: the `ScubaResults` file, the run's folder or the `-OutPath` folder. |
| `ScubaGear.MaxReportAgeDays` | `7` | Refuse results older than this. `0` turns the check off. |
| `ScubaGear.ProductNames` | ScubaGear's default | The products to check: `aad`, `exo`, `securitysuite`, `sharepoint`, `teams`, `powerplatform`, `powerbi`. |
| `ScubaGear.M365Environment` | detected | `commercial`, `gcc`, `gcchigh` or `dod`. When Maester is connected to the USGov or USGovDoD cloud, `gcchigh` or `dod`. |
| `ScubaGear.ConfigFilePath` | none | A [ScubaGear configuration file](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/docs/configuration/configuration.md), with its exclusions, omissions and annotations. |
| `ScubaGear.Parameters` | none | Further `Invoke-SCuBA` parameters, for example `{ "Organization": "contoso.onmicrosoft.com" }`. |
| `ScubaGear.OutputPath` | temporary | Where ScubaGear writes its reports. Kept when set; a temporary folder is deleted after the run, because it holds tenant data. |
| `ScubaGear.PowerShell` | `powershell` on Windows | The PowerShell that runs ScubaGear: `powershell`, `pwsh` or the full path of one. |
| `ScubaGear.ModulePath` | newest installed | Run the ScubaGear module at this path (its `ScubaGear.psd1`) instead of the newest one installed. |

## How results map

| ScubaGear result | Maester result |
| --- | --- |
| Pass | Passed |
| Fail (a `SHALL` policy) | Failed, severity High |
| Warning (a `SHOULD` policy) | Failed, severity Medium |
| N/A (a manual check, or one a third-party product can meet) | Skipped, with ScubaGear's reason |
| Omitted (in the ScubaGear configuration file) | Skipped, with the justification |
| Incorrect result (in the ScubaGear configuration file) | Skipped, with ScubaGear's own result |
| Error | Error |
| `-` (a policy removed from the baseline) | Not shown |

## Licence

ScubaGear is published by CISA under [CC0 1.0](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/LICENSE). This
pack does not include its code: it runs the module you install, or reads the results it wrote. The pack's catalog
of policy titles, rationale and remediation steps is generated from ScubaGear's baselines.

content.text:
I've built the ScubaGear pack in a new worktree on branch `worktree-scubagear-pack`, from `main`. Nothing is committed. Its own tests, the general repository checks and `Test-MtPack -Official` all pass on this Mac. It has never been run against the real ScubaGear on Windows, which is the next thing to test.

**How it works**

The pack is `maester.scubagear`, with code `SCUBA.M365`, and it's off by default. Each ScubaGear result becomes its own row, such as `SCUBA.M365.MS.AAD.1.1`. The ID leaves out the policy version (`v1`), so a row keeps its ID when CISA revises a policy. The pack gets results one of two ways:
- **Read results you already have:** set `ScubaGear.ReportPath` to the `ScubaResults_*.json` file, the run's folder or the folder above it. This works on any platform, and the pack refuses results older than seven days or for another tenant.
- **Let Maester run ScubaGear:** on Windows, the pack starts a separate `powershell.exe` process, runs `Invoke-SCuBA` there and reads the results it writes.
  - It signs in through ScubaGear's own sign-in window. If Maester is connected app-only with a certificate, it uses that app and certificate instead.
  - ScubaGear's output shows live in Maester's console.
  - A temporary output folder is deleted afterwards, because it holds tenant data.
  - On macOS and Linux it skips, with a message saying ScubaGear only runs on Windows.

**Moving to PowerShell 7 later** takes one setting change, `ScubaGear.PowerShell = pwsh`, once a ScubaGear release includes [cisagov/ScubaGear#2411](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/pull/2411). `build/scubagear/README.md` notes this.

**How results map:**

| ScubaGear result | Maester result |
| --- | --- |
| Pass | Passed |
| Fail (a SHALL policy) | Failed, severity High |
| Warning (a SHOULD policy) | Failed, severity Medium |
| N/A, Omitted, Incorrect result | Skipped, with ScubaGear's reason |
| Error | Error |

Each result shows the policy's rationale, remediation steps and links. These come from a catalog generated from ScubaGear's own baseline data (CC0 licence, 109 policies).

**Files:**
- [packs/scubagear/](packs/scubagear/): the manifest, the guide, the test family in [Test.SCUBA.M365.ps1](packs/scubagear/tests/Test.SCUBA.M365.ps1), and `catalog.json`.
- [build/scubagear/Update-MtScubaGearCatalog.ps1](build/scubagear/Update-MtScubaGearCatalog.ps1): rebuilds the catalog from a new ScubaGear version.
- [ScubaGearPack.Tests.ps1](powershell/tests/functions/ScubaGearPack.Tests.ps1) and a test copy of ScubaGear's sample results under `powershell/tests/fixtures/scubagear/`, cut down to one control of each result type.
- [MaesterTestSchema.psd1](powershell/assets/MaesterTestSchema.psd1): `SCUBA.` added to the reserved prefixes, so custom tests can't use it. That meant regenerating `website/src/data/test-builder.json`.
- A docs page, [scubagear.md](website/docs/packs/scubagear.md), and a list of the shipped packs in [index.md](website/docs/packs/index.md).

**Testing:**
- **Pack tests: 28 of 28 pass.** They read the test results file, and run a fake ScubaGear module in a child PowerShell process. These caught one real bug, now fixed: a `ScubaGear.ModulePath` that doesn't exist was reported as "ScubaGear 0.0" instead of "not installed".
- **General repository checks: 1,138 of 1,138 pass**, after regenerating the test-builder data.
- **`Test-MtPack -Official`:** the pack is valid. The security scan rates it High risk. That comes from running a ScubaGear the user installs themselves in a separate process, plus starting a process and calling commands by computed name.
- **One Zero Trust pack test fails on this machine, and the cause isn't this change.** Its "module not installed" test expects a skip. But the real ZeroTrustAssessment module is installed here, so the test ran the real assessment and got an error instead.

**Things to know:**
- **I chose the code `SCUBA.M365`.** That leaves `SCUBA.GWS` free if the ScubaGoggles pack comes back.
- **Running PowerShell in this session:** the worktree guard wouldn't let my shell start `pwsh`, so I ran each script in a Terminal tab set to the worktree and closed the tabs afterwards.
- **Not done:** ScubaGear's own HTML report isn't embedded in the Maester report. It's a set of linked pages, not one file, so I left it out.
